support_jen: Hey — multiple customers (CS#3542, CS#3548) reporting large p99 spikes for function/tool calls when structured-output + tool-router are both enabled. Started ~04:12 UTC after the recent canary. Example request id: r-9a7c3f. Anyone seen this before?

infra-bot: deploybot: canary deployed rtr-2026-04-12T04:10Z (commit abcd123). Notifying eng-runtime.

alex_s: grabbing traces now. First-pass: schema validation step (validator) latency jumped — p95 went from ~220ms to ~1.1s and p99 from ~520ms to ~2.4s on the tool/router path.

mona_r: Confirming metrics — router.queue_time.p99 spiked to ~600ms. Validator worker CPU usage looks normal but sys CPU and minor GC pauses increased. Could be a change in the validator library or larger payloads.

sre_paul: Sharing trace snippets: 
```
[trace] r-9a7c3f -> router -> validator.validateAsync() -> wait 1180ms -> serialize -> respond
[logs] validation-time=1180ms queue-time=420ms total=1600ms
```
Stack samples show node threads stuck in `v8::Execute` during validation. Any recent validator package bumps?

alex_s: There was PR #2210 that bumped `ajv` and switched to `validateAsync` for some heavy schemas. That landed in the canary at 04:10. Rolling back candidate: PR #2219 prepared. Short-term mitigation: flip feature flag `validator.async=false` to force sync path and avoid the new async behavior.

support_jen: Customer repro steps (copied from CS ticket):
```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-tool-1","input":"call:forecast","tools":[{"name":"forecast","schema":<very large schema>}] ,"stream":false}'
```
Observed response p99 ~2.1s. Request id r-9a7c3f appears in our logs.

mona_r: Quick local experiment: disabling schema validation for that route (feature-flag `route.X.validator=false`) reduced p99 to ~240ms. So validator is the bottleneck.

alex_s: Agreed. Proposed mitigations (short -> mid -> long):
1) Short: flip `validator.async=false` + rollback ajv bump (PR #2219) to restore previous behavior.
2) Short-mid: add heuristic to skip full validation for payloads >100 fields or depth>10 (feature flag).
3) Mid: autoscale validator pool + bounded queue + circuit breaker to avoid queue pile-up.
4) Long: move heavy schema checks to an async pre-validation pipeline (background worker) and allow a fast-path non-blocking response or fallback.

sre_paul: I'm applying hotfix now: increasing validator replicas from 3->6 and toggling `validator.async=false` in prod canary. Will watch p99 and queue metrics.

infra-bot: deploybot: hotfix rollup r-2026-04-12T04:45Z rolled to production canary; tag=r-rollback-2210.

support_jen: Customer reported back after hotfix: latency dropped to normal for their test cases — they confirmed :thumbsup:. I'll mark their tickets as mitigated pending follow-ups.

mona_r: Follow-ups to action: collect 1h heap+cpu profiles from validator pods around the incident, add a synthetic nightly CI job that runs the largest known schemas through the router to verify p99, and add alerting where validator.queue_time.p99>400ms for >5m.

alex_s: Created INF-472 (https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-472) to track rollback PR, hotfix, benchmarks, and the longer-term async validation redesign. Linking PRs: #2219 (rollback), #2235 (feature-flag heuristics).

support_jen: We'll close the customer escalations once INF-472 has stable monitors and we confirm no regressions in next 24h. Thanks everyone for quick turnaround.

mona_r: One extra note — add an integration test that simulates `tools[]` with deeply nested arrays; ajv upgrade revealed a pathological case where `validateAsync` yields event-loop starvation. We should guard the router against this class of work.

alex_s: Good point. I'll add an E2E that asserts router.p99 < 500ms for the heavy-schema scenario and a canary gate to block ajv/validator bumps without a perf benchmark.

sre_paul: Monitoring will track until 05:30 UTC; will update if any further anomalies.
